blocks.text: King Edward Village — Knight Street / Kingsway / East King Edward Avenue (Aquilini Group)

The development comprises 398 residences plus retail space across the ground and part of the second floor (retail-podium brokerage source); a City planning appendix describes the comprehensive development as buildings of 5, 7, 12 and 17 storeys. Construction is concrete and title is Freehold Strata (current listing at 4078 Knight Street: concrete construction, CD-1 zoning, Freehold Strata title, built by Aquilini Group); listings at 4028 Knight Street likewise record a concrete building in the Knight sub-area. Year built differs by source: listings record 2007 (4078 Knight Street) and 2008 (4028 Knight Street), while the retail-podium source records 2009 for the podium. The development was completed in phases and the strata plan for the specific building governs. Amenities and services at grade include the Save-On-Foods, the Vancouver Public Library branch and services in the podium (listing sources). Published rental position: a 4078 Knight Street listing describes the building as "Rental Friendly (Nothing Less than 30 days)" — consistent with the post-November 24, 2022 rule that long-term rental bans are void while short-term (under-30-day) restrictions can still apply. Pet restrictions: not confirmed from the sources checked — read the registered bylaws.
Streets, schools and getting around Knight

items.t: "Knight" is the Knight Street corridor in Vancouver East: the major north–south arterial running from the Clark Drive / Great Northern Way area south through Kensington-Cedar Cottage, Sunset and Victoria-Fraserview to the Knight Street Bridge over the Fraser River's north arm to Richmond. The City lists "Knight" as a recognised smaller area, but it is not one of the City's 22 distinct local areas.

Where the condo stock actually concentrates: overwhelmingly at one node — Kingsway / King Edward Avenue at Knight Street, where the King Edward Village development holds the corridor's apartment condos above its retail podium. Elsewhere the corridor's residential form is detached houses on the side streets, with townhouse infill (Knight 18, The Charles) on and just off the street, and commercial / mixed-use frontage on the arterial itself.
Cross streets that structure the corridor: East Broadway, Kingsway, East 33rd Avenue, East 41st Avenue, East 49th Avenue and SE Marine Drive.
Transit: the corridor is crossed by the R4 41st Ave RapidBus and the 41 at East 41st Avenue, the 49 at East 49th Avenue, and the 9 at East Broadway; no SkyTrain station sits on the corridor.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Knight

items.t: Area plans: the Kensington-Cedar Cottage, Sunset and Victoria-Fraserview / Killarney community visions apply to the local areas the corridor runs through, alongside the citywide Vancouver Official Development Plan, which replaced the Vancouver Plan on March 31, 2026; a Knight-corridor-specific adopted plan: Not verified. The June 2025 Conwest referral also records that Council repealed the Kensington-Cedar Cottage Community Vision in November 2023 — do not cite the old vision as current policy for the King Edward node.

The grocery store, library and bank are inside the condo development. King Edward Village's podium holds the Save-On-Foods, the Vancouver Public Library branch and services that listings describe as "right at your door step" — the amenity is the podium tenancy mix (the retail podium is 92.20% occupied in the brokerage source, with Save-On-Foods, TD, Service Canada and the library occupying 71.81% of it), so a change in podium tenancies changes daily life in the towers above.

Council's 2007 neighbourhood-centres report records the Knight and Kingsway plan adding capacity for about 800 further ground-oriented homes on top of the over-370 units on the King Edward Village site; the 2025 Conwest referral records that the Kensington-Cedar Cottage Community Vision that framed the node was repealed in November 2023. Policy citations for this corner need a date check.

The health centre is on the street itself. South Community Health Centre, 6405 Knight Street at East 49th Avenue, provides public and community health services for South Vancouver from an address on the corridor — one of the few civic anchors physically on Knight Street.

Knight 18's name and its phase count do not match — check the disclosure. The current 3430 Knight Street listing names the project "Knight 18" while recording 7 units in the development phase shown and a 2026 build year; a buyer needs the disclosure statement / strata plan to reconcile the full collection size before relying on either figure.
The corridor's south end is a bridge, not a boundary street.

items.t: Where the townhouse stock concentrates: at the corridor's north end, in Kensington-Cedar Cottage — Knight 18 at Knight Street & East 18th Avenue and The Charles at East 21st Avenue & Knight Street, both just off the Kingsway business district.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Knight

items.t: Form B diligence (Knight 18; The Charles if its tenure proves strata): Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page. For a 2026-built complex the Form B also settles which phase's strata the unit sits in — the document that reconciles Knight 18's name, phase count and unit count. Listing-level rental/pet lines in are listing data, not bylaws.

Fee-simple side-street product: That is the correct default frame for the corridor's duplex and multiplex homes; if The Charles' tenure proves fee-simple rather than strata, its diligence moves to this frame entirely — which is why the tenure question in is not a footnote.

Knight 18's name and its counts do not match — in three directions. The project is called "Knight 18" for its Knight Street & 18th Avenue corner; current listings record 7 units in the development; an older presale archive records 12. A buyer who assumes the name is the unit count, or that either published count is the whole project, is relying on marketing arithmetic — the disclosure statement is the only settled source.
The Charles was sold as a 2023 project and resold as a 2025 building. Price presale completion promises here accordingly.
The grocery store, library and bank for the corridor's condo node are inside the condo development.

Council repealed the Kensington-Cedar Cottage Community Vision in November 2023 (recorded in the June 2025 Conwest referral) — any Knight / King Edward marketing that cites the old vision as current City policy is citing a repealed document.

Side-street house lots: detached houses on the side streets east and west of the arterial, with commercial, mixed-use and strata product on the Knight Street frontage itself and at the avenue crossings. A fee-simple lot carries no strata, no Form B and no strata fees. Frontage position is the defining pricing fact: Knight Street frontage lots carry arterial exposure (truck traffic, noise) and price differently from side-street houses one block in — never comp one against the other without an explicit frontage adjustment.

Lot character: the residential side streets sit under the R1-1 District Schedule of Zoning and Development By-law No. 3575 — minimum site area 306 m² for a single detached house or duplex and for a multiple dwelling of 3 to 4 units (minimum frontage 10.0 m), 464 m² for 5 units (13.4 m), 557 m² for 6 to 8 units (15.1 m); a single detached house may include a secondary suite and a laneway house, and a multiplex may have up to 6 units or up to 8 rental units.
Serviced position: corridor homes are on City water and sewer services; a 2026 utility dollar figure confirmed on a City source: Not verified.

ALR vs non-ALR: ALR land inside the corridor: Not verified — no ALR parcel is confirmed and no split is stated. Flood position: the corridor's south end descends to the Fraser River's north arm at the Knight Street Bridge and the City's designated floodplain includes the coastal floodplain along the Fraser River in South Vancouver; parcels in it carry Vancouver Building By-law setback and flood construction level requirements.

No bare-land strata plan or community on the Knight corridor was verified: The corridor's strata stock is building-form strata (King Edward Village apartments; Knight 18 townhouses) — not bare-land strata.

King Edward Village — Knight Street / Kingsway / East King Edward Avenue (Aquilini Group). CD-1 comprehensively-zoned development site: one master-planned mixed-use development, with homes addressed across the podium at 4028 Knight Street, 4078 Knight Street, 1432 Kingsway and 1483 East King Edward Avenue. The development comprises 398 residences plus retail space across the ground and part of the second floor (retail-podium brokerage source); a City planning appendix describes the comprehensive development as buildings of 5, 7, 12 and 17 storeys. Construction is concrete and title is Freehold Strata (current listing at 4078 Knight Street: concrete construction, CD-1 zoning, Freehold Strata title, built by Aquilini Group); the retail-podium source records Zoning CD-1 (420). Sources differ on the year built — 2007 (4078 Knight Street listing), 2008 (4028 Knight Street listings), 2009 for the podium (brokerage source); the development was completed in phases.

Conwest proposal — 4001–4009 Knight Street and 1348 East 24th Avenue. Rezoning application, staff recommendation to REFUSE: An application to rezone from C-2 and RM-1 to CD-1 for a 23-storey mixed-use building containing 233 strata-residential units, a 37-space childcare facility and ground-floor commercial. City staff's June 3, 2025 referral report recommends the application be refused following the public hearing. A refused-recommendation proposal is not built stock and not land for sale — no buyer should price the corridor as if these 233 homes exist.

BC Housing supportive housing — 1406 and 1410 East King Edward Avenue. Proposed non-market housing, excluded: A proposed social / supportive housing building at Knight Street and East King Edward Avenue (12 storeys and approximately 90 studio homes with supports in the BC Housing fact sheet; a later application report describes a 14-storey building with 109 modular studio units) for adults, seniors and people with disabilities experiencing or at risk of homelessness, to be operated by non-profit housing societies. Non-market housing — not strata lots or homes for sale in any form.

items.t: Nearby areas: Fraser VE along Fraser Street to the west, Killarney and Champlain Heights to the east, Mount Pleasant and Riley Park to the north-west, and Richmond across the Knight Street Bridge to the south.

Civic anchors near the corridor: Memorial South Park, 5955 Ross Street, in Sunset west of the corridor; Sunset Community Centre on Main Street near East 49th Avenue and Killarney Community Centre, 6260 Killarney Street, are the nearest Park Board centres named; a community centre inside the Knight sub-area itself: Not verified. The South Hill Branch library, on Fraser Street west of the corridor, serves the west side; its civic address was not confirmed on a VPL page: Not verified.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Knight

items.t: Plans — local-area visions (one repealed) + Vancouver Official Development Plan: the Kensington-Cedar Cottage, Sunset and Victoria-Fraserview / Killarney community visions apply to the local areas the corridor runs through, alongside the citywide Vancouver Official Development Plan, which replaced the Vancouver Plan on March 31, 2026; a Knight-corridor-specific adopted plan: Not verified. Date-check any policy citation for the King Edward node: the June 2025 Conwest referral records that Council repealed the Kensington-Cedar Cottage Community Vision in November 2023 — do not cite the old vision as current policy for that corner.

Strata diligence (King Edward Village, Knight 18 — and any bare-land strata lot, if one is ever met here): Form B diligence (fees, amounts owed, levies, CRF balance, insurance summary; provided within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page) — at King Edward Village the depreciation report is also where podium, parkade and retail-interface obligations surface; depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws void since November 24, 2022 (short-term restrictions may still apply by bylaw — King Edward Village's "nothing less than 30 days" listing line is exactly that enforceable short-term form); only 55+ age bylaws valid under SPA ss.123.1/123.2, with May 1, 2023 exemptions (younger spouse/partner, caregivers, legacy residents, defined children); a listing's "45+" line is not a valid BC age bylaw. No corridor complex is published as 55+. For The Charles, tenure comes first: if it proves fee-simple, there is no Form B at all — title and City rules only.

The grocery store, library and bank are inside the condo development: King Edward Village's podium holds the Save-On-Foods, the Vancouver Public Library branch and services listings describe as "right at your door step" — the retail podium is 92.20% occupied in the brokerage source, with Save-On-Foods, TD, Service Canada and the library occupying 71.81% of it — so a change in podium tenancies changes daily life on the site above it.
Policy citations for this corner need a date check.

Knight 18's name and its counts do not match — in three directions: the project is called "Knight 18" for its Knight Street & 18th Avenue corner; current listings record 7 units in the development; an older presale archive records 12. The disclosure statement is the only settled source for the whole-project total.

The corridor's newest townhouse stock arrived about two years late: The Charles' presale sources state expected completion Summer 2023 in one place and Fall 2024 in another, while the first resale listing records year built 2025 — the same slippage pattern as Knight 18 (Spring 2024 estimates, 2026 build year). Price presale completion promises here accordingly.

The corridor's south end is a bridge, not a boundary street: Knight Street carries Highway 99 traffic over the Knight Street Bridge to Richmond — for north-end owners that is the Richmond/YVR route from the front door, and for side-street owners it is the source of the truck traffic priced as frontage exposure.

faq.a: At one node: King Edward Village at Knight Street, Kingsway and East King Edward Avenue — 398 residences in buildings of 5, 7, 12 and 17 storeys over a retail podium. The rest of the corridor is side-street houses and townhouse infill.
faq.q: Where are the Knight corridor's condos, actually?

faq.a: They are addresses within the one King Edward Village development by the Aquilini Group — listings under all four addresses carry the King Edward Village name. Price and compare them as one development's phases/faces, not as four competing buildings.
faq.q: Are 4028 Knight, 4078 Knight, 1432 Kingsway and 1483 King Edward different buildings?

faq.a: Sources conflict — 2007 in a 4078 Knight Street listing, 2008 in 4028 Knight Street listings, 2009 for the retail podium in the brokerage source — consistent with phased completion. The conflict is flagged in; the specific building's strata plan and Form B govern.
faq.q: What year was King Edward Village built?

faq.a: Long-term, yes — rental-restriction bylaws have been unenforceable since November 24, 2022, and the building is marketed as rental friendly with a nothing-less-than-30-days term, which is the enforceable short-term restriction. Vancouver's Empty Homes Tax declaration still applies if the unit sits empty.
faq.q: Can I rent out a King Edward Village condo?

faq.a: Read the registered bylaws in the strata package before writing. Pet bylaws remain enforceable in BC.
faq.q: Are pets allowed at King Edward Village?

faq.a: No legacy townhouse subdivision and no fee-simple townhouse complex was verified on the corridor.
faq.q: What townhouses can I actually buy on the Knight corridor?

faq.a: Not confirmed as a whole-project total. The name says 18; current listings record 7 units in the development as sold/marketed and the presale source describes 7 family-size townhomes in two 3-storey woodframe buildings; an older presale archive records 12 units. The disclosure statement and strata plan settle it — do not quote any of the three figures as the project total without them.
faq.q: Knight 18 — is it 7 homes, 12 homes, or 18?

faq.a: It matters: strata means a Form B, depreciation report and CRF; fee-simple means none of those, title and City rules only. Get the disclosure statement or a title search before writing an offer.
faq.q: Is The Charles strata or fee-simple?

faq.a: Only if that side is legally separate — a strata lot in a 2-lot strata plan, or its own fee-simple lot from a subdivision. None is verified by name here; a single-lot duplex sells whole. Check the title first.
faq.q: Can I buy just one side of a duplex on the Knight corridor?

faq.a: Fee-simple by default: No strata, no Form B, no strata fees — diligence is title, the R1-1 schedule and registered covenants. The strata frame applies only where title shows a strata lot.
faq.q: Strata or fee-simple — which frame applies to a side-street duplex here?

faq.a: Not one of the 22 distinct local areas — the City lists "Knight" as a recognised smaller area; the Knight Street corridor runs through the Kensington-Cedar Cottage, Sunset and Victoria-Fraserview local areas.
faq.q: Is "Knight" an official City of Vancouver neighbourhood?

faq.a: The Knight Street Bridge over the Fraser River's north arm to Richmond — the City frames Victoria-Fraserview as lying between the Knight Street Bridge and Killarney.
faq.q: What is at the south end of Knight Street?

faq.a: No station sits on the corridor in the sources read — the corridor is bus-served and crossed by the R4 RapidBus at 41st Avenue and the 49 at 49th Avenue, with the bridge carrying traffic to Richmond.
faq.q: Is there a SkyTrain station on the Knight corridor?
